The "01JSTE5S3DK3DATDJYF3SD013A" you gave is a Netlify Internal ID for a 404 (Page Not Found) error.
This means that the site you're trying to visit on Netlify exists, but the specific page or URL path doesn't — or maybe the site isn't properly deployed yet.

When Netlify gives you that 404 with an Internal ID, it usually means:

  • The domain (like wavingnotdrowning.netlify.app) is registered on Netlify.

  • But either:

    • The deployment failed.

    • The page you requested wasn’t set up yet (common when building a new site).

    • The DNS isn't fully connected yet.

  1. Check your Netlify Dashboard:
    Log into Netlify and look under "Sites". See if your "wavingnotdrowning" project is there.

  2. Confirm the build and deploy:
    If the site is listed, check if the latest build was successful or failed.

  3. Default page:
    Make sure you have an index.html (or your framework’s equivalent like index.js, home.vue, etc.) in your project — Netlify looks for it when loading your site.

  4. Domain settings (if you are using a custom domain):
    Ensure your domain (like wavingnotdrowning.com) is correctly pointing to Netlify servers (correct CNAME and A records).

In short:
✅ You have a site linked to Netlify.

🌎 What is DNS?

DNS = Domain Name System.
It’s basically the internet’s address book.

When someone types:

springheeled-jack.com

the DNS tells their browser:

"Oh! That domain points to the website files hosted at IONOS."

✅ Without DNS, your browser wouldn't know where to go when you type a domain.

🛠 What's happening with your DNS right now:

StepStatus
Domain is registered✅ Done
Domain connected to hosting✅ Done
DNS updates triggered✅ Done
DNS still propagating worldwide⏳ (this is the current stage)

✅ Your domain is connected to hosting, but
🌐 the DNS information is still spreading across the internet globally.

This can take 15 minutes to several hours.

📈 Why DNS takes time:

When you connect a domain to hosting:

  • DNS servers all over the world (like in London, New York, Tokyo, etc.) need to update their records.

  • Some servers update very fast (like in 10 minutes).

  • Some servers are slow (take 2–6 hours).

  • Your local network (your ISP) may cache old DNS data for a few hours.

✅ It’s not broken.
⏳ It’s just the internet catching up.

🔥 GOOD NEWS:

You don't need to do anything.
The DNS is updating silently in the background.

Soon, when you (or anyone) types:

arduino
https://springheeled-jack.com

➡️ The browser will know to go straight to your Spring Heeled Jack website!

  • Try from another device (like your mobile phone using mobile data) — sometimes mobile networks update faster!

  • Use a VPN and connect to a different country — sometimes you can see it live earlier!

  • Wait a little more (typical wait time: 15 minutes to 2 hours).

Here’s the exact guide to try and speed up DNS refresh on your computer.

🛠 How to Manually Force DNS Refresh (Windows):

Option 1: Basic Browser Hard Refresh

👉 Try this first (very easy):

  1. Open your browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, etc.).

  2. Press Ctrl + F5 together (on Windows).
    (This forces the browser to ignore its cache and reload fresh from the server.)

✅ Try visiting: https://springheeled-jack.com

Option 2: Flush Your Computer's DNS Cache

👉 If Ctrl+F5 didn’t solve it, do this:

  1. On your keyboard, press Windows Key + R.
    (This opens the Run window.)

  2. Type:

    nginx
    cmd

    and press Enter.
    (This opens the Command Prompt — a black window.)

  3. In the Command Prompt, type this command exactly:

    bash
    ipconfig /flushdns

  4. Press Enter.

✅ You should see a message:

Successfully flushed the DNS Resolver Cache.

What this does:

  • It forces your computer to forget old internet address information.

  • When you visit springheeled-jack.com again,
    your computer asks for fresh DNS info immediately.

⚡ Bonus Advanced Trick (if needed):

If you’re really impatient and want to check using external DNS:

  • Visit: https://dnschecker.org/

  • Type springheeled-jack.com

  • Choose "A Record"

  • Click Search.

✅ It will show you which parts of the world already have your domain live!

A 404 error ("Page Not Found") simply means:

The server is working, but it cannot find the page you're asking for.

🛠 Here's what this tells us:

ProblemCause
Server reachable (no connection closed)✅ GOOD
Files not found / wrong structure❗ PROBLEM

In simple words:
You uploaded something, but Netlify (or the server) can't find the right index.html in the right place.

🎯 What's happening technically:

On Netlify:

  • You must have your index.html in the root (top level) of your upload.

  • NOT inside another folder when you upload.

  • NOT zipped unless Netlify auto-extracts properly.

✅ If the index.html is missing or too deep inside folders, you get a 404.

📋 Step-by-Step Correct Fix:

Please trust me — let's do it slowly, manually, so it's perfect this time.

STEP 2: Upload ONLY the contents

✅ Drag the index.html file itself,
NOT the zipped file,
NOT the folder,
just the raw file index.html into Netlify’s "drag and drop" area.

This way, Netlify sees the index.html at the top level, and the website will load.

🚀 Deploying Your Static Website to Vercel

  6. Click on "Deploy".

If you're encountering issues where the browser attempts to download files instead of rendering them, this is typically due to incorrect MIME types or misconfigured static site settings.

🛠️ Troubleshooting Steps

1. Check MIME Types

Ensure that your static files have the correct MIME types set. For example, HTML files should have text/html as their content type. Incorrect MIME types can cause browsers to download files instead of displaying them.

2. Verify Static Site Configuration

In your Render dashboard:

  • Navigate to your service settings.

  • Ensure that the Publish Directory is correctly set (e.g., public or the directory containing your index.html).

  • Confirm that the Build Command (if any) is appropriate for your project.

3. Inspect File Structure

Ensure that your project's file structure is correctly organized. For a static site, your index.html and other assets (CSS, JS, images) should be in the root of the publish directory or appropriately referenced.

✅ Next Steps

  1. Review your Render service settings to ensure correct configuration.

  2. Check your project's file structure and MIME types.

  3. If issues persist, consider redeploying your site with the corrected settings.

If you need further assistance or a walkthrough of these steps, feel free to ask!
